meaningMnemonic: This radical is the same as the kanji. It means have .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means prefecture .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means think .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means tooth .

A leader asks half of his men to accompany him on a secret mission. The leader’s mission is volunteer only, so it’s impressive that he got half of his men to accompany him. Hints Imagine you are one of the leader’s men who volunteered. What made you want to accompany him? Imagine the good qualities of this leader and how he inspired you to accompany him on this mission.
readingMnemonic: The leader you decided to accompany is none other than Han ( はん ) Solo. Who could be more inspiring? I’m surprised not more than half decided to accompany him. Han Solo is awesome. Hints Imagine yourself as you accompany Han Solo. You try to stay calm, but you’re just so excited to be around Han Solo.

meaningMnemonic: You get tooth orders . You get these tooth orders various times in your life, depending on your age . Hints You get baby age tooth orders (to get your first teeth). You get child age tooth orders (to get your adult teeth). Then you get old age tooth orders (when you start losing your teeth). There are tooth orders for every age.
readingMnemonic: Gaining and losing teeth aren't the only things dependent on age . There is also an age in which you get your first ray ( れい ) gun. Hints Decide what age you have to be to get your first ray gun, and then imagine getting it when you hit that age. Perhaps you use this ray gun on your teeth, to keep them clean. Hint: when you see the radical orders it's fairly likely the reading will be れい .

meaningMnemonic: Take some leather and wrap your possessions in it. Now you have a bag to carry them around in. Neat! Hints Picture yourself carefully wrapping leather around a bundle of your things to make this bag. Look at you, being all DIY and stuff.
readingMnemonic: You actually learned this reading with the vocabulary word カバン . It's been a while though, so here's a mnemonic to help you connect it to this kanji: The reason you made your own bag is that there's been a car ban ( かばん ). With this car ban, you can't just throw all your stuff in your car anymore (come on — we all know you were using it like a second closet) so now you need a bag to carry it around in. Hints Thanks to this car ban, you were able to establish yourself as a successful maker of bespoke leather bags. Funny how the universe works out like that sometimes.

meaningMnemonic: By showing the roof of your top hat you send your best regards . Hints Giving your best regards is basically just tipping your hat and showing the roof of it.
readingMnemonic: When you give your best regards you always yell YOLO ( よろ ) to the other person. Hints YOLO means "you only live once," so in a way that's a good way to give your best regards. At the very least, it's an interesting way.

meaningMnemonic: Your mouth has a tooth that you use to bite and chew with. Hints Imagine that one tooth in your mouth chewing through everything. It's not easy to chew with only one tooth, but luckily yours is huge and razor-sharp, so it helps you to bite and chew your way through anything you like.
readingMnemonic: Your one tooth is so strong that you can even use it to bite and chew up a whole ca r ( か ). Hints Some people like eating cars, and you're one of them. You can't get enough of those delicious cars. You just bite them apart and chew.

meaningMnemonic: The more shellfish you have , the more you can bribe people. That worked in the olden days when shells were money, and today too if the people you want to bribe really like seafood. Hints Imagine bribing a bunch of yakuza and politicians with all the shellfish you have. Ohohoh, you'll never be caught!
readingMnemonic: Welp, the cops found out about your bribe , that didn't last long, and now your entire family is watching you get put into the police car screaming, " WHY ( わい )?! Hints Yeah really, why? Why bribe people at all. You could have just been rolling in shellfish dough. Why risk everything? And you counter with. Why not?

meaningMnemonic: Someone is offering you a shellfish in exchange for a kiss . This is a bribe ! You don't want to kiss them, but that shellfish sure looks tasty. Hints "Come on, don't you want this shellfish?" they ask, shaking it up and down at you.
readingMnemonic: You go through with the bribe and kiss the person, but then they snatch hold of the shellfish and run straight down the ro ad ( ろ ). No!! Hints This is why you never accept a bribe. One second you're staring a yummy shellfish in the face, and the next you're standing alone in the road feeling used.

meaningMnemonic: The door in that direction is among a cluster of doors. You run in the direction of the cluster and one door stands out to you. You enter it. Hints Imagine seeing all these doors, this cluster of doors. You feel confused at which one to enter but finally pick one. Hear the door creak as you open it.
readingMnemonic: After you make it through the door, you come across another cluster of doors. Which one to choose? There's a loud thunderous sound coming from behind one and you decide to open it. Behind it, there's an entire bow ling ( ぼう ) alley and people bowling, loudly! Hints Watch as clusters of pins fall when the bowling balls hit them. You back up and peek through one of the other doors in the cluster and it also houses a bowling alley. Huh.

meaningMnemonic: A tiger needs to think and consider its actions before it attacks. Tigers are smart hunters, so they need to consider all options and really think through a situation. Hints Look at this tiger as it approaches you. Think what things it has to consider. It has to consider how big of a threat you are and so on. And you need to consider how you're going to escape from this tiger.
readingMnemonic: Finally, the tiger speaks: "I'm consider ing going to Rio ( りょ ). Have you ever been?" Hints Imagine your relief when you realize this tiger isn't considering you as prey, but is considering whether to visit Rio de Janeiro and just wants your advice. There are no tigers in South America, so I guess it's natural for one to consider Rio in its vacation plans.

meaningMnemonic: They say if you put things on a slide , seven things to be exact, that’s the best way to consign goods to someone. They say if you consign seven things to someone, you should send them over on a slide. Slide ‘em on down. All seven of ‘em. Hints Imagine what seven things you consign over to this other person for safekeeping. Visualize them in your head as you slide each one down the slide.
readingMnemonic: One of the seven things you consign over to this guy is a tack ( たく ). It’s the sharpest tack you’ve ever seen. You slide the tack down the slide. Good thing no one is on the slide now, sitting on that tack would hurt. Hints Let’s imagine what it would be like to hit this tack while sliding on the slide. It would hurt. Good thing you are consigning it over to someone. Probably safer for everyone that way.

meaningMnemonic: Past stamp s usually depict images contrary to current views. Hints Look at this stamp. There's Columbus being hugged by a bunch of South American natives. Yikes, that's contrary to how things went, that's for sure.
readingMnemonic: Don't be the type of person who acts contrary to how they should and instead be like Kyaku ( きゃく ) the customer. They're always so nice and polite and they don't give diseases to entire populations of people. Hints Be contrary to the evildoers of the past and be like Kyaku instead.

meaningMnemonic: The kind of thread you'd wrap around someone would have to be a cord . A regular thread wouldn't be strong enough, so you'd definitely use a cord. This can also mean connection , since cords create connections (by tying things together). Hints Imagine taking that cord and wrapping it around someone (with their permission, of course). Feel your fingers tightening a knot in the cord. Then tie the other end around yourself. Is this some freaky ritual to deepen your connection to them, or… ? Hey, no judgment from me.
readingMnemonic: Actually, you're tying this cord around someone as part of a show ( しょ ). What kind of a show? I really shouldn't say. This cord show isn't free, I'll tell you that much. Hints Imagine doing this cord show on stage. Feel the heat of the stage lights and the gaze of the audience as your tie your cord. What are they expecting? Why did they pay to see this? Must be some kind of modern performance art — let's go with that.

meaningMnemonic: In the rain I take my rake and shake it, making a demand that the rain stop! I demand this rain stop right now! Don’t make me shake my rake more violently than I am currently shaking it! Hints Go out into the rain and shake your rake. Imagine shouting your demand at the sky as the rain pelts you from above.
readingMnemonic: Now imagine the rain changing. Wait a second, this isn't rain, it's ju ice ( じゅ )! You shake your rake harder, and demand that the juice rain continues. It doesn't listen to your demands and stops as soon as you start bottling it. Well, at least you have enough for one, really small juice box. Hints Picture yourself demanding more rain from the sky, trying to fill up your tiny juice box with what little juice rain you were able to get.

meaningMnemonic: You offer a hot pepper to the king , and he gives you a drop of something. You look down at the drop to see it transforming into a disc . And not just any old disc at that. It's a jade disc . Have you ever seen ancient Chinese jade discs with holes in the middle? That's what this kanji is referring to. Hints You took a long time to pick out the perfect hot pepper. Only the best for the king, right? It burned your hands a little as you held it on your way to the palace. You were hoping for something pretty special in return, but you never imagined it would be a drop that magically turns into a disc. Wow!
readingMnemonic: You look closely at the disc and realize the hole in the middle is actually a keyhole. You fashion a key out of hay — a hay key ( へき ) — and shove it in. You rotate the hay key until you hear a click. The jade disc opens. Hints Imagine the riches contained in the jade disc, all revealed because of your special hay key. You look up to see the king smiling at your amazement.

meaningMnemonic: A mole in winter will do whatever you ask, if you know how to ask it. Hints They do most of their own chores during the rest of the year, so winter is when you should ask them to do things for you.
readingMnemonic: To get the mole to do what you want, just give it a nice big hunk of chee se ( ち ). Hints Moles will do anything for cheese, but honestly, wouldn't we all?

meaningMnemonic: You're on a scooter and suddenly someone throws a hot pepper at you and you have to dodge it. Hints Imagine riding your scooter, dodging multiple hot peppers as they're tossed at you. A few of them get stuck in the wheels and keep coming around and around, and you have to dodge them too.
readingMnemonic: As you dodge the hot peppers, you feel a strong he at ( ひ ) fill your body. You can't tell if this heat is from the effort from dodging or if you didn't dodge right and one of the hot peppers touched you. Or maybe the scooter is overheating. Hints Feel the heat flow through your body. It's getting harder to dodge as the heat grows and you start sweating!

meaningMnemonic: With your fingers you pluck some flowers in a rice paddy , in order to draw them. Have you ever seen rice paddy flowers? They're beautiful. And if you can draw them, you can capture that beauty and show it to everyone. Hints Imagine using your fingers to draw these rice paddy flowers. Don't worry about how well you can draw. These flowers will look beautiful no matter how you draw them.
readingMnemonic: Even though you tried to draw the flowers as best you could, whenever someone looks at it they smell B.O. ( びょう ). Maybe it's because you were drawing for a really long time and kept sweating. Maybe it's because you are just a stinky person. But no one wants to look at your drawing for long because all they can smell is B.O. Hints To be fair, would you want to look at a drawing that makes you constantly smell stinky B.O.? I didn't think so.

meaningMnemonic: You got your copy of "The Dry Knife ." It's the newest edition of the magazine you love on keeping your knives dry. Hints You're really into this magazine, and when you heard there's a new edition of it, you went out and bought it right away.
readingMnemonic: In this edition of "The Dry Knife," there is a huge article written by Genghis Khan ( かん ) on how he kept his knives dry while campaigning. Hints The article on Genghis Khan was perhaps the best written article in the Dry Knife series to date. How did this magazine get such a big interview?

meaningMnemonic: You use your scooter when the omen comes so that you can escape . Hints Unfortunately, the omen is riding a scooter too, so you're going to have to be crafty to escape this omen properly.
readingMnemonic: You decide to escape this omen by weaving in and out of the busy streets of とう きょう . By now, you know とうきょう like the back of your hand, so you're sure you can escape this way. Hints Imagine scooting in and out of とうきょう traffic, the omen looming ever further back behind you. You're doing it! You're escaping!

meaningMnemonic: Where do you put your fingers when you're on an escalator ? On the handle ! Okay, so maybe it's not a handle and more of a railing, but for the sake of this kanji, picture a handle instead. Hints Imagine being on an escalator and wrapping your fingers around a small handle on your way up or down. It's still a bit precarious, truth be told.
readingMnemonic: You put your hand on the handle and an old person leans in close to you and says, " 暑か ?" ( あつか ). He wants to know if the handle is ... hot? Before you can respond he says it again, and again! “ 暑か？！ 暑か？！？！ 暑か？！？！？！ ” he's shouting as you slowly ride the escalator away from him. Hints 暑か ? Is the handle hot? Think about it. Is it? What does your imagination tell you?

meaningMnemonic: If there’s a drop on your head and the rice is big , you know you’re in the interior . And by interior, I mean you’re actually inside someone. The rice is big because you’ve shrunk to a tiny size and are inside someone’s stomach. The drop on your head is actually digestive fluid. Hints Imagine being in the interior of someone’s tummy. See the big pieces of rice all around you as drops of stomach fluid continue to drop down on your head.
readingMnemonic: While you’re in the interior of this guy, you hear him break out in song. He starts singing “ Ok lahoma” ( おく ) at the top of his lungs. The big pieces of rice slosh around as he sings and dances. “OOOOk-lahoma, where the wind comes sweepin' down the plain!” Hints If you’re unfamiliar with this Oklahoma song, check it out on YouTube. Imagine being in the interior of someone’s belly as you hear this song booming all around you.

meaningMnemonic: A leader with horns takes a lantern and searches for people to join him. He needs more people to join his cause so he can get his horns removed. He’s embarrassed of them which is why he only travels at night, hence the lantern. Hints Imagine this shady leader approaching you in the night. The lantern light shines in your face. Would you join him?
readingMnemonic: The leader guy approaches you out of the darkness, his lantern held high. Oh no, not that guy. You've heard about his horn problem and you don't want to join him. You look around and spot a large hay stack ( へい ). You quickly jump into it and hide from him. Hints The last thing you wanted to do was join that guy so you hid in a haystack to avoid him.

meaningMnemonic: Under the moon beneath a tree there is a hat filled with water . You stare down into the water and decide to stick your knee in it. Hints Feel the water splash over your knee as you stick it into this hat. It fits really well, the hat is the perfect size for your knee. Now look up at the moonlight filtering through the tree above.
readingMnemonic: Suddenly, in your knee , you feel he at and a za p ( ひざ )! Your knee is simultaneously burned and electrocuted by the hot water!! Hints Imagine the heat then the zap going through your knee. It isn't a nice heat, it's a hot heat, then BZZZT zap! Your knee was heat zapped pretty bad.

meaningMnemonic: You change this geoduck because you want it to lean . Right now it's standing up straight, but you want it to lean to one side instead. Hints Why do you want this geoduck to lean? Try to come up with your own reason. And why don't you look up what a geoduck looks like one more time for good measure. You don't want to be able to get this image out of your head.
readingMnemonic: To get the geoduck to lean you put a piece of ca ke ( けい ) on one of its sides. Hints Watch as the geoduck slowly leans toward the cake, trying to get at it for a taste. But don't let it eat any! Keep putting the cake further and further away so the geoduck has to lean more.

meaningMnemonic: The thread on this football is loose . We need to tighten up the loose thread on this football or it’s gonna fall apart while we’re playing. Hints Look at this football. The thread is loose on the football and needs to be tightened. Attempt to tighten the loose thread on the football as you hold it in your hands.
readingMnemonic: You finally tighten the loose thread and all of your friends cheer, “ You ru le!” ( ゆる ) You rule because you fixed the loose thread on the football and now you can play again. Yeah! You rule, man! Hints Listen to your friends shouting “You rule!” and hear their cheers echo in your ears as you toss the football around again.

meaningMnemonic: When the director wants to see what's going on with his subordinates, he has to peek at them secretly. Hints The director's employees and underlings are all going to be on their best behavior if they know he's watching, so he has no choice but to peek at them through binoculars and hidden peep holes and stuff.
readingMnemonic: What does the director like to peek at most? The inside of people's nose s ( のぞ ). This director's kind of a weirdo, and he gets a kick out of peeking inside his subordinates' noses. Hints Imagine the director alone in his big, fancy office, peeking inside the noses of all his staff members with microscopic surveillance cameras. What a nosy guy.

meaningMnemonic: When it's spring in heaven they play music . To your mortal, human ears it sounds more like snow melting, birds chirping, and plants waking up. Hints Close your eyes and imagine all of the spring sounds that come down to you from heaven in the springtime. Mmm, you can almost smell the damp soil and rain.
readingMnemonic: In heaven, the ones that play music are the sou ls ( そう ) of the dead. They have a huge band up there, and even though it just seems like normal spring sounds to you, up there in heaven when the souls play music it's more like a huge, 100-part band! Hints Picture all of the souls in heaven playing spring music together!

meaningMnemonic: A woman who has a landslide getting ready inside her is pregnant . And that baby is gonna come out like a landslide. Hints Picture an ultrasound of the pregnant woman, but instead of a little baby heartbeat, you hear a scary roaring sound. That's what being pregnant is like. Waiting for the landslide to come.
readingMnemonic: When you're pregnant the baby is constantly kicking you with their shin s ( しん ). Not their feet, their shins. And shins are really hard, let me tell you. Hints Imagine being pregnant and getting kicked by the shins of your baby all day, but especially all night. You're so tired. Please let this landslide come already.

meaningMnemonic: A woman sleeps with the king and becomes pregnant . Only the king wasn’t human and now the woman is pregnant with a hybrid alien baby! Hints The king radical is slightly altered in this kanji, so just remember that the king is a strange alien and not human. Imagine being this woman and having this half-breed alien baby inside you. Feels weird.
readingMnemonic: Being pregnant with this strange creature, you need to do something to calm you down. You should play Nin tendo ( にん ). Nintendo really calms your nerves and makes being pregnant with some mutant baby not seem like that big of a deal anymore. Hints What game are you playing on the Nintendo? Maybe it’s a game where you kill alien invaders? That’s messed up.

meaningMnemonic: You put on the shellfish mask once per year and break into people's beach houses, leaving behind presents . Hints You're like beach santa, except you're real and you wear a mask made of shellfish.
readingMnemonic: The " presents " you leave? They are actually just zo mbies ( ぞう ). You leave zombies in people's houses. Hints Ooh hoo, it's me! the Shellfish Mask Man! I go to beach houses and leave presents where I can! The presents are not clothes, or anything good. I don't even care if you leave me some food. Try whipping some up, try cooking me peas, It matters not, I'll leave you zombies! Tee hee hee hee hee!

meaningMnemonic: Shove your fingers into a bowl of shrimp to select the best one. You know your shrimp and you know them well, so you won't settle for anything less than the best. Put your whole arm in there and feel around until you can select the one you want most. Hints Feel your fingers touching each and every shrimp, one by one, until they graze the one you select as the perfect shrimp. Slowly pull it out and lower it into your mouth. Munch munch... ahhh! The perfect shrimp.
readingMnemonic: You do this at every restaurant, party, and indoor sporting event and people start getting wise to your shrimp select ion methods. One day, as you attempt to select your shrimp, a sharp pain shoots through your finger. Ow! You pull your hand back to find... a tack ( たく )! Hints Oh, woe is me! How will I select the perfect shrimp with my fingers if there are tacks in the shrimp bowls! Boohoohoo!

meaningMnemonic: There's a scooter coming toward you with a net trapping a weird zombie on it. You don't want this here, so you decide to send back the zombie. (It's a weird zombie because it has the ground on top of its head instead of dirt!) Hints You want to send back this zombie the way it came. You definitely don't want it loose in your neighborhood.
readingMnemonic: As you prepare to send back the zombie, you imagine yourself as Genghis Khan ( かん ). On your horse (it's just your own scooter) you stab forward with your spear (stick), swing the scooter the zombie is on, and send it back from whence it came! Hints You managed to send back the zombie, good for you! Genghis Khan would be proud.

meaningMnemonic: You have thread and some syrup and you need to spin them together. Drip the syrup onto the thread and spin it around and around over your head. Hints Imagine carefully dripping syrup onto a thread and then spinning it in a circle.
readingMnemonic: As you spin the syrup, it begins to change shape and forms into a coo kie ( く )! Haven't you ever made syrup-spun cookies before? The spinning forms and cooks them in the air. Hints Imagine eating a syrup cookie you made by spinning it yourself. Homemade is always better than store-bought.

meaningMnemonic: Use your fingers on the cat pirate to suppress him. The cat pirate was attacking you, so you took your fingers and pet his head and scratched his chin. Now he's calm and suppressed. He doesn't even remember why he was attacking you. Hints Imagine suppressing a cat pirate with your own fingers. His fur is so soft, but his nails are so sharp!
readingMnemonic: He forgot, but you know you had to suppress the cat pirate because he was trying to steal your egg yolk ( よく ). You were making breakfast on your ship and the cat pirate boarded you out of nowhere, and tried to take it by force. Hints Defend the yolk! Smell the smell of eggs in the air as you suppress the cat pirate. Maybe even share the yolk with him, once he's done trying to kill you for it. And then enjoy breakfast while petting your new cat friend.

meaningMnemonic: In your prefecture , you come from a long lineage of people who share one heart . When the heart is passed on to the next in line, it flies out of their body, and suspend s itself in the sky, for you to take. Hints You see the suspended heart in the distance, and make your way towards it.
readingMnemonic: You arrive at the suspend ed heart. There in front of it, protecting it, is Ken ( けん ) the samurai. Hints "I've protected this suspended heart for you, for you are next in the lineage to receive it." He grabs the heart and throws it into your body.

meaningMnemonic: You take a grain and fashion it into a gun that is small , earning you the title of Small Arms Dealer (or SAD). Congratulations! Hints This isn't exactly a title you're proud of, in fact, you're really embarrassed. Maybe you can make a name for yourself in something else so you can get a new title.
readingMnemonic: Word of your SAD title makes it all the way to the Shou gun ( しょう ) and he travels out to see you. When he arrives at your door, with all of his fancy escorts, he hands you a plaque with your title on it. Hints The plaque says, "No one is more deserving of this SAD title." - Love, the Shougun.

meaningMnemonic: Your boat holds your weapon like a plate . So in a way, it's just a tray for your weapon. Hints A big boat shaped like a plate is just a tray. You keep your weapons on it, nice and flat.
readingMnemonic: Unfortunately, this boat tray is so huge, it's gotten you ban ned ( ばん ) from the Small Boat Tray Association. Those pesky small boat tray enthusiasts... Hints Your ban from the Small Boat Tray Association has led to a massive feud between large boat tray enthusiasts and small boat tray enthusiasts, and it seems like it'll never end—leading to bans all over the place. If only we could all come together as enthusiasts of boat trays of all sizes...

meaningMnemonic: 馬鹿 is "stupid" so if you hear a rumor about something ( らしい ) that's stupid, you'll just respond by saying "that's absurd ."
readingMnemonic: The reading comes from 馬鹿 .

sentences.japanese: 全く馬鹿らしいにもほどがある！！！
sentences.english: That’s completely absurd!!!

meaningMnemonic: Remember how you learned that 馬鹿 means "idiot?" Well put two idiots together and everything they say and do is absolutely absurd . Remember how ridiculous that "Dumb and Dumber" movie was? Yeah. Like that.
readingMnemonic: You already learned 馬鹿 , so as long as you can remember it twice in a row, you should be able to read this too!

sentences.japanese: 馬鹿馬鹿しいこと言わないでよ。
sentences.english: Don’t say stupid things.

meaningMnemonic: To 頼む is "to ask for" or "to request." The noun version of that is a favor or a request .
readingMnemonic: The reading comes from 頼む .

sentences.japanese: コウイチはビエトに窓を開けるよう頼みましたが、ビエトはコウイチの頼みを拒絶しました。
sentences.english: Koichi asked Viet to open the window, but Viet turned down Koichi's request.

meaningMnemonic: A cool cluster is something that has a cluster of cool-creating coolant. This device is air conditioning .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 暑すぎだよ〜。ちょっと冷房付けてもらえないかな。
sentences.english: It's too hot. Could you turn on the air conditioning please?

readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own. Just remember that 合 is read as ごう here. Who orchestrated this annexation ? Good ol' grandpa ごういち .

sentences.english: The United States of America annexed Texas the year I was born.

meaningMnemonic: 及ぶ means "to reach" or "to amount to." The noun version is more like a grammar thing, as it means " as well as ." Perhaps if you are reaching a certain point or certain amount, then you are adding things on. That's why this means "as well as". Note that 及び is a term usually used in formal writing.
readingMnemonic: The reading comes from 及ぶ , so if you know that one you know that one as well as this one.

sentences.japanese: このセキュリティー対策アプリは、AndroidOS及びiOSのどちらでもご利用頂けます。
sentences.english: This security app is for Android OS as well as iOS.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same, so this means bag . You actually learned the kana version of this word already: カバン . In casual writing, it's often just written in kana, but the kanji version is fairly common too. You'll especially see it in commercial settings — store signs and ads, for example — or in literature with a more grown-up vibe.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as the one you learned with the kanji and with カバン .

sentences.english: to put down a bag

sentences.english: to put into a bag

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means accompany , so the verb vocab version is to accompany or to be accompanied by . This word is both transitive and intransitive. So it works both when bringing someone with you, like 助手を伴って来る (to come with an assistant), or when going along with someone else, like 上司に伴って行く (to go with one's boss). When it's about physically accompanying someone, it's often used together with a movement verb. 伴う is also used figuratively to talk about consequences that tend to go hand in hand with something, like 変化にはリスクが伴う (change comes with risk). In this case, 伴う is usually used by itself.

sentences.japanese: うちのお父さんは、マフィアのボスだと疑われて、FBIに電話を盗聴されたことがあるんだよ。
sentences.english: My dad was once suspected of being a mafia boss, and his phone got wiretapped by the FBI.

sentences.japanese: 誰かがトーフグのオフィスに盗聴器を仕掛けたのですが、私達は犯人も理由も分かりません。
sentences.english: Someone bugged the Tofugu office, but we have no idea who or why.

meaningMnemonic: A temporary title is what you give something when you don't have a final title for it. it's a working name or a tentative name .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: この建設中のショッピングモールの仮称知ってる？
sentences.english: Do you know the tentative name of this shopping mall under construction?

sentences.japanese: タイトルはまだ単なる仮称です。
sentences.english: The title is just a temporary name for now.

sentences.japanese: トーフグが仮称だったなんて、びっくりだよ。
sentences.english: I was surprised to learn that Tofugu was just a working name.

meaningMnemonic: When you lack stretch ing, your body has to get that energy out somehow, so you end up yawning .
readingMnemonic: The reading for this is an exception. Here's a mnemonic to help you: You've never seen more yawning than when you performed acu puncture ( あく ) on a bee ( び ). It was so relaxed from being the one poked for once that it just couldn't stop yawning.

sentences.japanese: 退屈すぎて欠伸が出てきた。
sentences.english: It was too boring and I yawned.

meaningMnemonic: Your year age is the number of years old you are.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 「年齢はおいくつですか？」「あまり言いたくないです。」「じゃあ、別にいいよ。ただ、百歳を超えてるかどうかだけ教えてくれない？」
sentences.english: "How old are you?" "I’d rather not say." "Okay, then. Just let me know if you are older than 100."
